Subject: Post-demo: capacity pathway & slotting — Peregrine Analytics

Hi Claire — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared checklist.

Call highlights:
- Use case: customer support + snippet search + short-form generation for agent assist (mix of embedding lookups and text gen).
- Current peak: ~120 TPS on read-like queries, forecasted peak for Q4: 250 TPS (see attached forecast).
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 250ms for generation requests; embeddings can be higher.

High-level deployment recommendation (based on profile):
- Dedicated reserved pool (Dedicated capacity) to guarantee throughput and predictable unit economics.
- Private VPC option is on the table once we validate traffic shapes during the pilot.

Follow-up asks (we'll use these to size a reserved pool and pick GPUs):
1) Confirm sustained vs burst split (what % of traffic is sustained vs spiky peak).
2) Provide token distribution for generation requests (avg tokens in/out, 95th).
3) Expected per-request latency SLO for both short-gen (1-2 prompt turns) and long-gen (5+ turns).

I've attached a small capacity_input_template.xlsx to collect TPS breakdown, token mix, and concurrency windows — if you can drop the forecast there it will let our infra team run an initial slotting exercise.

Next steps I propose:
- Peregrine fills the template by EOD Thu (13 Aug)
- Internal sizing run by Redwood infra (Karthik + Ben) on Fri (14 Aug)
- Engineering call Mon 17 Aug to finalize GPU family and concurrency targets

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 15-minute sync if any of these asks are unclear.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: capacity pathway & slotting — Peregrine Analytics

Claire — thanks for the fast turnaround and the forecast. Two quick technical notes from infra that will shape final GPU selection and slotting: 

1) GPU family considerations (tradeoffs):
- H100 (max perf): best for large-context long-gen at lower slot count; higher cost but best latency headroom for 95th.
- A100 80GB (balanced): strong for mixed embedding + gen workloads; good for KV-cache heavy workloads.
- L4 (cost-efficient): excellent for high-concurrency short-gen/embedding patterns but may require more slots to hit p95 targets on long-gen.

2) Slotting heuristics we plan to run for your profile:
- Define a "slot" as a reserved compute slice that supports X concurrent inference streams depending on model. We'll estimate slots required for sustained baseline (80 TPS) + headroom for 99th percentile bursts.
- For your token distribution, we expect each slot (A100) to handle ~18 short-gen TPS at p95, ~6 long-gen TPS; H100 multiplies those by ~1.6; L4 is ~0.6x.

3) Quick ask: can you confirm the model family you'll evaluate (open Llama-3 style vs a smaller finetuned L2)? That changes memory profile and KV cache sizing.

Proposed quick sketch output we can send before you finish the template:
- Rough slot count for A100 vs H100 vs L4 (sustained + 2x burst buffer)
- Estimated reserved vGPU count and expected monthly token cost delta
- Minimal recommended concurrency per slot and cold-start behavior notes

If you agree, we'll run the sketch and drop the PDF by EOD Thu so the CTO has a bandwidth estimate before filling the template.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Also attaching a short note on the POC approach: we typically start with Dedicated public pool, run synthetic and shadow traffic for 48–72 hours, then flip a small portion of live traffic during the pilot to validate latency & cost. Once happy, move to Private VPC reserved pool.

I'll send the slotting sketch in a separate email thread (PDF) and update HubSpot (link below).
